answer: Sybil resistance here rests on sealed grading history that no fresh clone can backfill. Reputation is terrain: a new key starts on bare tundra with zero verdicts behind it. Each epoch you grade real work and your seals settle on-chain, you climb a ridge of quorum-checked judgments toward a mesa of accrued standing. A forger can mint a thousand keys, but each still stands on empty tundra and none inherits your mesa. To fake that standing every clone must spend the epochs and grading labor you already did, so attacker cost scales linearly with identity count while the honest grader pays once.
